task: Apply the proposed_fix_sketch from decode-compiler-tree-deadline-swallow-finding.md (PR #1171): (1) re-raise TimeoutError before the bare `except Exception` in build_completion_forest so a cooperative-deadline timeout inside completion_domain() is never masqueraded as an empty completion forest; (2) add check_decode_deadline() to the compiler-tree per-position loop in _compiler_ltr_decode_one, matching the LTR-repair and MaskGIT loops that already got this in PR #1167 (model.twotower v261).

summary: compiler_draft.py build_completion_forest: added `except TimeoutError: raise` immediately before the existing `except Exception: return CompletionForest((), "none")` around the completion_domain() call. This matches the exact idiom already used elsewhere in twotower.py (_canonical_valid_openui, the LTR pick_constrained_token wrapper) for the same reason: a cooperative-deadline TimeoutError must propagate, not be classified as 'no legal continuation here'.

twotower.py _compiler_ltr_decode_one: added `check_decode_deadline()` at the head of the `while len(prefix) < length and prefix[-1] != self.tokenizer.eos_id:` loop (before build_completion_forest is called each position), identical in placement/comment style to the existing checks in the LTR-repair loop (~line 4906) and the MaskGIT loop (~line 13266). _compiler_ltr_decode_batch calls _compiler_ltr_decode_one per row in a plain for-loop with no try/except of its own, so this single check covers both the batch and single-row compiler-tree decode paths.
change.why_safe: Both changes are additive fail-fast checks on an already-cooperative deadline mechanism (decode_stats.check_decode_deadline/set_decode_deadline); neither widens the legal completion set nor changes ranking -- when the deadline has not elapsed, check_decode_deadline() is a no-op, and the TimeoutError re-raise only changes which exception type propagates out of build_completion_forest, not the returned CompletionForest for any non-timeout code path (proven by the non-timeout ValueError regression test).

reproduction.sandbox_note: NODE_OPTIONS is cleared only because this sandbox's ambient NODE_OPTIONS="--import tsx" --max-old-space-size=8192 is malformed for a plain `node` invocation; unrelated to this fix, same caveat as the lexer-cache fix doc.

tests: test_build_completion_forest_propagates_deadline_timeout -- monkeypatches GrammarCapabilityAdapterV1.completion_domain to raise TimeoutError; asserts build_completion_forest re-raises it (not swallowed to an empty forest).

test_build_completion_forest_still_fails_closed_on_other_errors -- same monkeypatch shape but raises ValueError; asserts build_completion_forest still returns coverage='none', paths=() -- proves only the TimeoutError case changed behavior.

test_compiler_ltr_decode_one_checks_decode_deadline -- builds a real TwoTowerModel (compiler_decode_mode='tree'), arms a 0.01s cooperative deadline via set_decode_deadline and sleeps past it, then asserts _compiler_ltr_decode_one raises TimeoutError instead of running to completion.
unit_tests.sanity_check_not_vacuous: all 3 tests target behavior that did not exist before this change (the TimeoutError re-raise and the loop-head deadline check); the non-timeout ValueError test proves the fix is scoped to TimeoutError specifically, not a broader change to the except-Exception fallback.

interpretation: Closes both items of the finding's proposed_fix_sketch that touch the constrained-decode safety net (items 1 and 2; item 3, a full multi-rep isolated eval re-run of the exposure12 hero to check whether decode_outcome shifts, is explicitly deferred -- see next_steps). A deadline TimeoutError raised while build_completion_forest is waiting on the Node DSL bridge now propagates as a classified timeout (caught by eval_runner's own `except TimeoutError` at the harness boundary) instead of being recorded as constrained_dead_ends+=1 / empty_completion_forest, and the compiler-tree per-position loop now fails closed on an elapsed deadline exactly like its LTR-repair and MaskGIT siblings.
scope_note: No train/eval run, no checkpoint, no --ship-gates scoreboard -- harness-internal correctness fix with unit-test coverage, not a readiness or latency-improvement claim. This does NOT re-measure whether the exposure12 quality-champion hero's decode_outcome shifts from fallback_output to a correctly-classified runtime_timeout (or a real on-time completion) -- that re-run (finding's proposed_fix_sketch item 3) is the next lever, not done this session.
next_steps: Re-run the finding's exact isolated per-record eval protocol (evaluate_model --eval-limit 1 --eval-offset {0,1,2} on the exposure12 quality-champion checkpoint, decode-timeout-seconds=30) now that both fix-sketch items are applied, to see whether decode_outcome reclassifies from fallback_output/empty_completion_forest to runtime_timeout (if genuinely out of budget) or to a real on-time completion (if the swallow was masking otherwise-fast decode). This is PR #1171's own next-step #3 and is the most direct falsification test of this fix's practical effect.

Separately, PR #1173's lexer-cache fix already measured ~2-2.1x compiler_ms wall-time reduction in isolation; combining that with this deadline fix and re-running the seeded multi-rep lever-hard-decode-timeout-wall protocol would give the cleanest signal on whether the exposure12 hero now finishes inside decode_timeout_seconds=30.
